Abstract

Firesetting is a common behavior that is frequently encountered by forensic mental health experts when consulting on criminal and civil legal cases. Despite its prevalence, minimal attention has been paid in the literature to conducting firesetting-related forensic evaluations. In this article, we discuss the differences in the behavior of firesetting, the crime of arson, and the diagnosis of pyromania. The literature on adult firesetter characteristics, classification systems, recidivism, and treatment is reviewed. Several types of common criminal and civil firesetting-related evaluations referred to forensic mental health experts are discussed, along with case examples illustrating how the courts have approached such assessments. To our knowledge, this article is the first in 20 years to address firesetting-related forensic evaluations within the psychiatry literature. Shin Hae-chul (; May 6, 1968 – October 27, 2014) was a South Korean singer-songwriter and the frontman, vocalist of rock band N.EX.T. He was a record producer known for being a pioneer of Korean experimental rock music. He was referred to by fans as the "Demon Lord" or "The Devil" for his charismatic stage presence.

Shin and his band Muhangwedo debuted at the 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, where the band won first place for the song "To You." He formed the experimental rock band N.EX.T in 1992. He was also known for hosting a radio show from 2001 to 2012.

Shin died as a result of medical malpractice after undergoing surgery in 2014.

Early life

Shin Hae-chul was born on May 6, 1968. He enrolled in Sogang University in 1987, where he studied philosophy until he dropped out to focus on his music career.

Career

Debut

Shin formed the band Muhangwedo () in 1988 when he was a sophomore at Sogang University. The band received national attention when it appeared on the televised 1988 MBC Campus Music Festival, a singing competition for amateurs. Muhangwedo won first place for the song "To You" () which was written by Shin. The band released one album, 1989's When Our Lives Are Almost Over ().

Early solo career

Shin released his first solo album in 1990, which included a song that had an English rap, which was unconventional in the Korean music scene at the time. The album was a huge hit, leading to Shin rising to the top of Korean pop music charts and receiving multiple Korean pop music awards. His second solo album, Myself, was released in 1991, which was first album in Korea to have used midi. He also started a gig as a radio DJ on MBC FM.

The N.EX.T years

In 1992, Shin formed the band N.EX.T — moving from pop music to rock. Their first album, Home, was a concept album. While his previous songs were mainly about love or heartache, here Shin started to write more about social issues, such as criticizing the fast lifestyle of urbanites in "City People". The group's second album was released in 1994 titled The Return of N.EX.T Part 1: The Being where Shin introduced more philosophical lyrics, such as questioning the meaning of life in the song "The Ocean: About Immortality". The band's third album, The Return of N.EX.T Part 2: World. Some of the band members changed over time, with Shin being the constant lead singer/songwriter.

During this time he also did a one-time collaboration with singer Yoon Sang to form Nodance, wrote the original sound track for the Korean movie Jungle Story, and was the DJ for the MBC FM radio program FM Music City from 1996 to 1997. In 1996, he created his own label, Big Bang Music.

In 1997 N.EX.T released a rock ballad single, "Here, I Stand for You" which sold 500,000 copies in South Korea. (The lyrics of this song are engraved on his tombstone). The band went on to release their fourth album Lazenca: A Space Rock Opera in November 1997, which was also the original sound track for the television animation series Lazenca. The band split up after this- Shin went on to study music producing in London.

Crom

In London, Shin re-named himself Crom (inspired by Cromwell) and released a techno album Crom's Techno Works in 1998. The following year, he formed a project group Monocrom with guitarist Chris Tsangarides and released the eponymous project album Monocrom. The music in the album was experimental, combining heavy metal with Korean folk music, rap, and lyrical rock ballads. Most of the songs in this album were in English, which he collaborated with lyricist D. Yvette Wohn. After the release of Monocrom, Shin went to New York where he worked on producing his live album and some Korean movie soundtracks. In 2000, he created a three-man band Wittgenstein to produce a home studio album of the same name. He also wrote the song "Zergs are Coming" for the StarCraft music album.

Return of N.EX.T

Shin returned to Korea in 2002 and worked on various projects, mainly writing songs for other artists or for movie soundtracks. In 2004, he re-formed the group N.EX.T although the members were different, and released a double album The Return of N.EX.T Part 3: 개한민국. He also started DJing for a late night radio show Ghost Nation that became extremely popular. In 2007, N.EX.T released a jazz album The Songs for the One inspired by his newborn daughter. In 2008, the band released the album 666 Trilogy. After a long break, the band's final album, Reboot Myself was released in 2014.

Producer

Shin participated in special project in 2004, with the best musicians of Korea, the album named as
"Tribute to Park Nohae's Collection of poems The Dawn of Labor 20th anniversary". It is the first attempted project which the recordings dedicated to poetry in the history of Korean music. And he sang "Heaven" () with Psy on this album.

Radio DJ

Throughout his career Shin hosted several radio programs, including Music City with Shin Hae Chul신해철의 음악도시, distributed by MBC, April 1996~September 1997, served as 'the 1st Mayor' and GhostStation with Shin Hae Chul신해철의 고스트스테이션, by SBS, April 2000~March 2003, The matrix of MBC's 'GhostNation'. After supporting and campaigning for the president Roh Moo-hyun in 2002 election, Mr. Shin hosts the popular Ghost Nation on MBC, a late-night radio program since 2003. His fans call him "Mawang" (마왕 'the Demon Lord').

On September 16, 2007, Shin ended Ghost Nation. But he also announced that the broadcasting will be continuously served through the web, but no more broadcasting through MBC.

Personal life

He married Yoon Won-hee () on September 29, 2002,Singer Shin Hae Chul married in Japan(Korean), Yonhap, Retrieved on September 29, 2002 just before the 2002 election. He released his first jazz album The Songs for the One in 2007, dedicated to his wife and daughter.

Shin was found to be suffering from prosopagnosia, on a TV show (MBC Goldfish) in which he made a guest appearance.'Mawang' Shin Hae Chul suffering from prosopagnosia (Korean), Dailyseop.com, Retrieved on February 22, 2007 After that, he hosted a brand-new TV comedy debate program 100-second Debate (since May 2007), with a similar format of the MBC's 100 Minute Debate.Shin Hae Chul hosts '100-second Debate'(Korean), Yonhap, Retrieved on April 21, 2007 On July 29, 2007, he appeared as a victim (guest) of Lee Kyung-kyu's Hidden Camera.Even Shin Hae Chul encounted Molrae Camera (Korean), Hankook Ilbo, Retrieved on July 30, 2007

Death

Shin was treated for gastrointestinal problems by Dr. Kang Se Hoon at Sky Hospital on October 17, 2014. Kang carried out stomach reduction surgery without consent from Shin. During surgery, Kang punctured Shin's upper small intestine and pericardium, which later resulted in peritonitis. After developing a fever, which he was told was normal after surgery, Shin suffered a heart attack on October 22, and died on October 27 from peritonitis, pericarditis, sepsis, and brain damage due to lack of oxygen. At the urging of friends, Shin's family stopped his cremation at short notice and requested an autopsy. In March 2015, Songpa police found that Shin Hae-chul died from medical malpractice. Kang was struck off the medical register, fined and sentenced to one year in jail. The death of Shin through malpractice led to a revision of the law in South Korea to allow a state-run agency to help in malpractice cases. The law is referred to as the "Shin Hae-chul Law."

Tributes

Psy's song "Dream" was released in 2015 as a tribute to Shin. The lyrics were based on "talks with him about philosophy and death while drinking with him" which he answered "maybe all our lives might be a dream". Thus the profits from the particular song were planned to be donated to his bereaved family.

Shin Hae-chul's surgeon sentenced to prison

Published: 30 Jan. 2018, 20:01

It's been more than three years since the singer Shin Hae-chul died, but on Tuesday a court sentenced Kang Se-hoon, the surgeon responsible for Shin's death in 2014, to one year in prison.

Kang, the former director of the Seoul Surgical Hospital in Songpa District of southern Seoul, performed a laparoscopic surgery on Shin after the late singer visited the hospital and complained of a severe stomachache on Oct. 17, 2014. He died 10 days after the surgery. The family of the singer accused the doctor of professional negligence and took him to court in November 2016.

On Tuesday, the Seoul High Court revoked the primary ruling, and sentenced Kang to a full year of imprisonment as opposed to the initial sentence of 10 months of prison and two years probation.

The court also ruled that posting medical information about the patient on the internet is illegal, a charge that the first trial threw out citing that "leaking information about a dead patient is not going against the law."

"A series of perforations were formed either during or after the surgery performed by the accused," ruled the court on Jan. 30.

"[The surgeon] should have looked for the cause of the pain if the patient had complained of severe pain after two days of treatment, not prescribe him painkillers. Instead, he didn't take appropriate measures," the statement continued.

Shin went under a gastrolysis treatment on Oct. 17, then was admitted to the hospital on Oct. 22 suffering from a high fever and severe stomach pain. The singer died on Oct. 27, 2014.

1. outline
A song festival for college students hosted annually by MBC , it first debuted in 1977 and was held every year until 2012 .
2. history

In 1977, the Grand Prize Soldings Sandphebles- 「What should I do」

1977 On September 12 , one time was held at the Cultural Gymnasium, and Sand Pebbles won the championship.

Taking the freshness and wholesomeness unique to the campus in contrast to the established music world as the main concept, it aroused a great public response from the first stage, and later became an opportunity for numerous song festivals to flourish in earnest. However, the 'soundness' that the government thought at the time was overshadowed, and the student movement at the time viewed the college song festival with a bad eye because it promoted commercialism or decadence. Accordingly, the Jeondaehyeop - Hanchongryeon held a An alternative event called 'Unification Song Festival' was held. brunch material

Prior to the 1990s , the college song festival was literally a 'door to entry' to discover new musicians. At that time, the music industry was just starting to happen, and there was no regular growth and debut process for musicians. Musicians were selected by a small number of producers after building a reputation by performing at universities or some clubs. However, due to the rather weak media system and the changing circumstances of the times, the people's longing for art was great, and the MBC University Song Festival, a program led by public broadcasting, has established itself as a song festival with overwhelming authority.

All you have to do is meet the conditions of being a college student , so you can check the list of winning prizes regardless of the university's region or rank . The universities they graduated from are widely distributed, from Seoul National University to local universities in Gyeongsang-do or Jeolla-do, and like the case of Caterpillar , the members are the same. Groups with graduates from other universities can participate, without having to go to different universities. In addition, international students and Koreans studying abroad at universities in the United States , Japan , etc. are also eligible to participate. Before the finals, a separate regional preliminary round was held, which was hosted and broadcast separately by local MBC .[3]

In the first session, besides the original songs of the students, many adapted songs participated, but after that, it was gradually filled with self-composed songs. In the early days, an LP version was issued for each competition, but as the era was the era, as mentioned above, wholesome songs, songs by other established singers, and songs from other rounds other than the participation songs of the corresponding song festival were inserted without fail. A typical example is when the 1st prize-winning song and participating song were released as a record, Ham Joong-ah 's 'Love to Me' was also included. People who are not familiar with the situation mistake Ham Joong-ah for being a graduate of the college song festival.

It was an event with a strong image of youth and romance in that it was a stage for college students , and it was difficult to go to college with the goal of only the college song festival.[4] It was to the point where there were even college students who took a back seat to their studies. Like this, until the 1980s, young university students gave diversity to the Korean music industry with crude yet innovative musicality full of amateurism, and the college song festival filled the vacuum of rock bands in Korea, which were the wave of world music. Peregrine Falcon and Magma were hard rock/metal bands that were launched in this wave.

The filming location was also held indoors, such as the Cultural Gymnasium or Seoul Sports Complex indoor gymnasium , but with PD Joo Cheol-hwan 's idea , the 18th episode in 1994 first took place on the campus ( Korea University ), and later it became a trademark of the college song festival to be held on the university campus.

Because the college song festival has a long history and played a big role as a gateway to singers, many MCs and new singers gained fame through this contest, and many of them are still active in broadcasting houses to this day. Award winners from the 1970s and 1980s are invited back to the special stage for the n-year anniversary of the University Song Festival, where they present new award-winning songs, and occasionally remake award-winning songs or hit songs from terrestrial music programs such as Open Concert or I Am a Singer . . A semi-essential level for a compilation album with a concept that stimulates the nostalgia of the 70s and 80s generation .

Even if you look at the musician's side of the university song festival. Sanwoolim , Shim Soo -bong , Songbolmae , Roh Yeon , Kim Hak -rae , Won Mi -yeon , Yoo Yeol , Lee Mu Song , Shin Hae -cheol , Joo Byung -sun , Lee Jung -seok , Kim Kyung -ho , Kim Dong -ryul , etc. The names of the singers who were enjoying the times were revealed to the world through the university song festival.

Past MCs are also famous people , starting with former SM Entertainment Chairman Lee Soo-man, Myeong Hyun-sook, and the first Bomi unnie Wang Young-eun, just to name a few.[5] , Lim Ye-jin , Lee Deok-hwa , Kim Hee-ae , Lee Moon-se , etc. This is a part that gives an idea of ​​the status of the MBC College Song Festival. From 2003 to 2011, even though the man changed, Lee Hyori did not change.
3. Declining, discontinuing, and reviving
Early college song festivals received positive reviews for novel songs and discovery of new artists, and were criticized for commercializing college students .[6]

In the 1990s , excessive commercialization and the holding of competitive music festivals led to criticism of the decline in quality.[7] Even after that, the public's indifference was pointed out, and the main reasons for this were the change in university culture, the dilution of university characteristics, the change in public taste, the diversification of the music industry, the loss of authority in the music festival, and the absence of original songs with strong experimental nature.[8][9]

At the time of the university song festival , it was common for the talented people who polished their skills in the underground to go straight to the music industry, but in the 90s, the era changed so much. When the record industry became a business , and Lee Soo -man 's SM Entertainment, the MC of the Line and the University Song Festival , began to prosper from this time, the idol singers who had their support on their backs had a great success . all. From this period, a system was developed in the name of a trainee , and the system was developed . Competitive companies captured the public at once, leaving salty profits, and the funds and technologies that came from being able to reach an irresistible state.

On the other hand, the college song festival was still maintaining its past reputation, but it was losing out to established music that was relatively corporate, and the number of singers who were suddenly selected as stars through the song festival began to decrease to the point where only a handful could be counted. College students, who were largely pushed aside by the emerging system that seemed like a fountain of water and had no chance of receiving training in terms of skills, were not able to capture the public's attention with amateurism alone. It is correct to say that university song festivals after this period were maintained by the passion of artists for diversifying university culture and creation rather than industrial logic.

In addition, the university atmosphere and the social atmosphere were far removed from each other. Until the 1980s, universities had a strong image of being a gathering of selected intellectuals, and the social participation and collectivist behavior of conscious students began to disappear in the 1990s. After the reorganization of the 6th Republic of Korea , the political scene became more stable, and activist groups began to decline, and college students began to shift their interest to personal achievement and romance rather than social participation. In addition, entertainment venues such as karaoke rooms , video rooms , comic shops , and PC rooms had pushed out the college song festival from the culture. # 7080 The college entrance rate, which had stayed in the 10-30% range at the time, began to soar in the 90s and reached its peak of 83% in 2008, so college students who were intellectuals (except for high-ranking universities) were reduced to mere bridesmaids, and this is the result of the above . It completely changed the atmosphere of the university and even had the effect of eliminating the halo effect of the university. The status of the college song festival was inversely proportional to the college popularity rate.

The decisive decline in the college song festival began in the 2010s when audition programs such as cable broadcasts became huge hits. These audition programs judged only singing, not original songs, and broadened the scope of participation by targeting the entire country, and were able to gain greater public popularity than the MBC College Song Contest, which targets only a very small number of college students who can compose music . Shin Hae-chul was born on May 6, 1968. He enrolled in Sogang University in 1987, where he studied philosophy until he dropped out to focus on his music career.

Shin formed the band Muhangwedo () in 1988 when he was a sophomore at Sogang University. The album was a huge hit, leading to Shin rising to the top of Korean pop music charts and receiving multiple Korean pop music awards. His second solo album, Myself, was released in 1991, which was first album in Korea to have used midi. He also started a gig as a radio DJ on MBC FM.

In 1992, Shin formed the band N.EX.T — moving from pop music to rock. Their first album, Home, was a concept album. While his previous songs were mainly about love or heartache, here Shin started to write more about social issues, such as criticizing the fast lifestyle of urbanites in "City People". The group's second album was released in 1994 titled The Return of N.EX.T Part 1: The Being where Shin introduced more philosophical lyrics, such as questioning the meaning of life in the song "The Ocean: About Immortality".
